proof: P22R1 pins the acceptance packet to one exact reviewed commit, proves the pinned reviewer before the packet is sent, treats a no result as terminal, and makes the committed record verifiable without model credentials, while keeping exactly one reviewer and one verdict.

verification.command: bun run build && bun run package:check
bun run review:accept:negative-control (62 pass, 0 fail across acceptance-packet-secrets, acceptance-review-packet, acceptance-review-record, and acceptance-primary-transport)

bun node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit --strict --skipLibCheck --module ESNext --moduleResolution Bundler --target ES2022 --types bun --lib ES2023,DOM .agents/skills/questpie-v4/scripts/acceptance-review-packet.ts .agents/skills/questpie-v4/scripts/acceptance-review-record.ts .agents/skills/questpie-v4/scripts/acceptance-review-safety.ts .agents/skills/questpie-v4/scripts/acceptance-review.ts .agents/skills/questpie-v4/scripts/bounded-review-process.ts .agents/skills/questpie-v4/scripts/claude-acceptance-primary.ts .agents/skills/questpie-v4/scripts/verify-acceptance-review.ts tests/unit/acceptance-primary-transport.test.ts tests/unit/acceptance-review-record.test.ts tests/unit/acceptance-review-packet.test.ts (tests/** has no root tsconfig and is not covered by check-types, so this slice pins its own)

bun run review:accept:v2 -- --manifest docs/v4/prototypes/acceptance-determinism/acceptance-manifest-v2.json --dry-run (decodes the committed v2 manifest, resolves 7 packet documents, verifies every pinned authority digest and ancestry, and scans for secret-like material with no model call. The reported packet digest is deliberately not pinned here: the manifest is itself a packet document, so a digest recorded inside it could never match the packet it describes.)

acceptanceCriteria: A committed manifest owns the exact diff base, review output path, proof heads, ordered authority paths with SHA-256 digests, PASS-only deterministic gates, and acceptance criteria; a caller selects no model, effort, provider, axis, prompt, or authority file.

Every packet byte is read from the exact reviewed commit through git show rather than the working tree, authority digests must match, and a dirty worktree, an escaping or symlinked output path, a Git administrative attributes file, or an empty diff fails closed before any model call.

The diff is canonical: prefixes, rename detection, algorithm, context and inter-hunk context, an empty order file, an empty attributes file, and GIT_ATTR_SOURCE are pinned, so no local Git configuration can reorder, elide, or reshape what the reviewer reads.
Authority documents, the manifest, the diff, and the record are scanned for secret-like material, and a match refuses the run rather than redacting it.

The pinned reviewer proves itself before the packet is sent: it must report a version and declare every pinned option in its own help output. An absent or argument-rejecting reviewer is a distinct fail-closed error, never a review outcome, because such an invocation could never have produced a verdict.

A reviewer that could have answered and did not is a terminal NO_RESULT that writes no artifact, carrying a bounded, secret-scanned, single-line transport diagnostic so its provenance is auditable. No fallback transport exists and no second provider is introduced.

The committed record binds ticket, manifest path, reviewed head, diff base, packet digest, sanitized primary disposition, verdict, and timestamp, and verify-acceptance-review.ts re-derives the packet from the reviewed commit and validates it with no model credentials, failing closed on tampering, output replacement, or a non-PASS aggregate.
The revision adds no production Runtime behavior, no public QUESTPIE API, no provider registry, and no reusable model-selection seam; it is repository-quality internals only.
Protocol v1 evidence and the accepted v1 wrapper remain untouched and valid, and this slice is reviewed by that accepted wrapper rather than by itself.
